review.posthog_relevance: Ingestion warning and metric configuration for misrouted AI events, distinguishing them from other ingestion errors.
review.reason: The chunk demonstrates a substantive, bounded improvement in ingestion reliability and observability. P1.F7.H6, P1.F7.H7, and P1.F7.H8 show the implementation of a lane-based drop gate and the corresponding counter and warning emission, establishing the behavior and checks. P1.F2.H1 and P1.F3.H1 provide the warning definition and documentation. P1.F4.H1 and P1.F9.H1 are comments or
review.uncertainty: The chunk lacks the complete implementation of the `drop_misrouted_events` function and the full replacement of the old event drop path, which prevents establishing a Tier 3 systemic risk reduction. The tier is established on the visible ingestion-side gate and warning configuration, not on the complete removal of the old path.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the implementation of the new `drop_misrouted_events` function, the definition of `is_ai_lane_name`, or the complete replacement of `drop_non_ai_events`. It also lacks the corresponding changes to the ingestion warning emission and the complete removal of the old `drop_non_ai_events` function. Without these, the tier cannot be established.

observations.code_quote: | `misrouted_event`      | Event posted to the wrong v1 endpoint: an `$ai_`-prefixed name on `/i/v1/analytics/events`, or a name without that prefix on `/i/v1/ai/events`. A per-event drop inside a 200, so the rest of the batch still publishes | The event is well formed and only its destination is wrong. On v1 the caller picks an endpoint per event: `$ai_*` names go to `/i/v1/ai/events`, everything else to `/i/v1/analytics/events`. The `path` detail says which way the misroute went |
